The evidence, and why it is paper only
Tested on NSE 2005–2020, data it had never seen, with its rules fixed first: 33,979 trades, +0.21% a trade after futures charges, t 4.66, positive in every 5-year period but shrinking (+0.40%, +0.31%, +0.14%); it lost −0.48% a trade in the 2020 COVID crash. Found on 2020–2026 (+0.30% then +0.13% a trade). Not yet checked with the full deflated Sharpe. On paper since 2026-10-05: 45 trades, −0.073% a trade, 42.2% winners — a verdict needs 100 trades and 3 months (about early January 2027). One trade is about +0.2% on average and can lose several percent on a rally day; it works only over many trades. Real money on Zerodha only after a PASS.

UNTESTED — WATCH ONLY — 82 futures rows. Not a suggestion. Tap to see them.
If you take every row here (20 units each, before GM's charges): ₹33,14,908 in total; if every stop is hit, −₹49,730 — more if prices gap through the stops.
Most rows are in: Financial Services 14, Automobile and Auto Components 11, Healthcare 10. Rows in one sector tend to fall together. With no trend, a row's target comes before its stop at most as often as its break-even (about 37.5%) — a price with no trend is a fair game — so before GM's charges these rows make money only if the BUY signal works. It was tested and FAILED: the desk’s own rating, replayed day by day on six years of NSE’s own prices (2,36,746 stock-days), bought on this tab’s limit, target and stop, made −0.028% a trade after charges, 36.7% winners where 37.5% are needed (32,725 trades, t = −0.44).
BAD-DAY RISK, every row together — 1 day in 20: −₹42,508 or worse · worst day: −₹1,66,498 · market opens 5% lower: −₹1,60,740
Today’s 62 rows (20 units each) replayed through each of the last 496 trading days, Thu, 17 Oct 2024 to Fri, 16 Oct 2026, on real prices, with every stop and target in the market. Not a forecast: these are days that already happened. Before charges.
1 day in 20: on the worst 25 of those 496 days, all the rows together lost at least ₹42,508 — ₹57,411 on average.
Worst day, Mon, 7 Apr 2025 (NIFTY −3.24%): 62 of 62 stocks fell and 62 stops were hit, 61 of them by a gap at the open — a loss of −₹1,66,498, against −₹49,730 if every stop had filled at its own price (before charges).
Market opens 5% lower: −₹1,60,740. Each stock opens lower by its own measured sensitivity to NIFTY (median 0.96), and a stop fills at the open, not at its own price.
Together: on those 25 worst days, 94.1% of the stocks fell at once. These rows are closer to one bet on the market than to 62 separate ones.
Most of the bad-day loss: PAGEIND 20.3%, FORCEMOT 14.4%, MARUTI 7%, BAJAJ-AUTO 6.3%, EICHERMOT 4.8% — at 20 units each, the highest-priced stocks carry the most rupees.

Most of the bad-day loss: FEDERALBNK 5.9%, ICICIBANK 5.7%, AXISBANK 5.4%, SBIN 5.2%, HAL 4.8%.
Demergers, bonuses and splits are read from NSE’s own filings (Sun, 18 Oct 2026), so none of them counts as a crash.
For calls these figures are the pessimistic end. Each call is repriced with Black-76 at its own implied volatility, held where it is — and in a crash that volatility jumps, which cushions a call (India VIX moved +66% on Mon, 7 Apr 2025). By how much depends on each stock’s own option volatility, which this page has no history for.
Only on the stocks the desk rates BUY or ACCUMULATE — one side per stock, the side its analysis points to.
These options are priced from NSE’s 2026-10-16 settlement file, a session older than today’s last trades (2026-10-19). NSE publishes the 2026-10-19 file after about 19:00 IST, and the next build after that uses it. The futures tab already uses today’s last trades.

Puts — you BUY the put, it pays if the index or stock FALLS

NO TRADE — nothing on this tab has passed a test, so there is nothing here the desk can call a suggestion. Every rule tried on six years of NSE data failed (TRACK and the notes below have the numbers). The put rows under the fold are untested ideas, scored on paper on TRACK. Watching them costs nothing; trading them is a guess.
UNTESTED — WATCH ONLY — 79 put rows. Not a suggestion. Tap to see them.
If you take every row here (one lot each): ₹12,34,227 in total; if every stop is hit, −₹6,22,235 — more if prices gap through the stops.
These 79 rows are on 18 stocks: several strikes of one stock are one bet, not several. Most rows are in: Financial Services 36, Capital Goods 17, Metals & Mining 6. Rows in one sector tend to fall together. With no trend and fairly priced options, a put is expected to lose about its charges: about −₹6,655.98 across all 79 rows, one lot each, plus the bid-ask spread, which is not known without a live book (79 of these rows). 54 of 79 are priced above their own recent movement (implied above realised), which makes it worse. They make money only if the fall continues, and selling NIFTY in these downtrends failed its pre-registered test (final year t = 0.205).
BAD-DAY RISK, every row together — 1 day in 20: −₹4,16,996 or worse · worst day: −₹7,38,958 · market opens 5% higher: −₹9,29,922
Today’s 79 rows (one lot each) replayed through each of the last 496 trading days, Thu, 17 Oct 2024 to Fri, 16 Oct 2026, on real prices, with every stop and target in the market. Not a forecast: these are days that already happened. Before charges.
1 day in 20: on the worst 25 of those 496 days, all the rows together lost at least ₹4,16,996 — ₹5,05,321 on average.
Worst day, Wed, 8 Apr 2026 (NIFTY +3.78%): 18 of 18 names rose and 74 stops were hit, 64 of them by a gap at the open — a loss of −₹7,38,958, against −₹6,16,764 if every stop had filled at its own price (before charges).
Market opens 5% higher: −₹9,29,922. Each name opens higher by its own measured sensitivity to NIFTY (median 1.12), and a stop fills at the open, not at its own price.
Together: on those 25 worst days, 96.2% of the names rose at once. These rows are closer to one bet on the market than to 18 separate ones.
Most of the bad-day loss: CANBK 15.5%, AUBANK 9.8%, BANDHANBNK 9.3%, ABB 8.6%, LTF 7.7%.
Demergers, bonuses and splits are read from NSE’s own filings (Sun, 18 Oct 2026), so none of them counts as a crash.
For puts these figures are the OPTIMISTIC end. Each put is repriced with Black-76 at its own implied volatility, held where it is — but a put loses on the days the market rises, and on those days implied volatility usually falls, which takes still more off a put (India VIX moved −20% on Wed, 8 Apr 2026). The real loss on such a day can be larger than shown.
The stock puts lean on the desk’s SELL and REDUCE ratings, and those were tested: shorting them LOST. Replayed on six years of NSE’s prices, shorting every SELL/REDUCE row on this desk’s limit, target and stop made −0.139% a trade (35,236 trades, t = −3.31 — reliably negative), and over 20 sessions those stocks did slightly BETTER than the market. They are shown because you asked for the falling names, not because the rating picks fallers.
These options are priced from NSE’s 2026-10-16 settlement file, a session older than today’s last trades (2026-10-19). NSE publishes the 2026-10-19 file after about 19:00 IST, and the next build after that uses it. The futures tab already uses today’s last trades.

Hit rate counts only trades that filled and then finished. IF RANDOM is how often the target would come before the stop if prices moved at random — each trade's break-even, before charges. Only a hit rate above it, over enough separate bets, is evidence of an edge. The touch odds the desk showed ignore the stop, so they always run higher. Futures returns are GROSS per unit; options are NET of every charge per lot. ALL has no average return (futures move about 1.5%, options about 50%), and its money is options net a lot plus futures at 20 units, gross.

HOW THIS IS SCORED. Every price this page freezes is bought on paper at the moment it is shown. Each build then checks the market, using the day’s high and low so a move between two builds is not missed. Every ambiguity counts against the record: a target and a stop in the same window is a stop; a target in the same window as the fill is not counted; a gap through the stop exits at the open; a fill is always at the limit, never better; a price from before the level was shown can never fill it. Unfilled day orders die at 15:30. Futures are held at most 20 sessions; options until expiry. Stored in the private repository under docs/ledger/, committed on every build, and copied to the Google Sheet.
WHERE THESE PRICES COME FROM. Option premiums are from NSE’s 2026-10-16 settlement file (NSE posts the 2026-10-19 file after about 19:00 IST; the next build uses it); futures NOW is the 2026-10-19 last trade. The market was in its pre-open when this was built, so nothing here is executable right now. Premiums and the futures prices they are measured against both come from that same settlement file, so they describe the same moment. Not checked against NSE on this build (before the open, NSE's quote pages still show the previous session). Broker login OK from the build server at 2026-10-19 09:13 IST — a NIFTY quote came back. F&O ban for 2026-10-19: AMBUJACEM, KAYNES, SAIL — left out entirely, because NSE allows only exits in a banned stock. This page is a snapshot, rebuilt on a schedule — it is not a live feed. Check the price on your broker before placing anything. Net figures are after brokerage, STT at 0.15%, exchange, stamp and GST; the spread is extra and is only known where a live book was seen.
NO SHOCK SHIELD. Nothing on this page stops buys on a bad global morning — not a GIFT Nifty gap, a crude or S&P move, or an India VIX spike. Those signals were tested on NSE’s own data and failed (or had too few events to test), so they do not gate anything. Check the market yourself before acting on a shock day.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. That any of it makes money. The paper ledger so far: futures 29 targets and 149 stops, 16.3% hit (95% range 6.1–26.5%); short futures 14 targets and 43 stops, 24.6% hit (95% range 11.5–37.6%); calls 228 targets and 706 stops, 24.4% hit (95% range 13.9–34.9%); puts 1003 targets and 926 stops, 52% hit (95% range 34.5–69.5%), over only 16 sessions of the same market. That says how this market went, not that a rule works — each row shows its own break-even. And every test fixed in advance so far, on data never used to build the rule, found no edge: the desk's own rating (replayed on six years of NSE data: −0.03% a trade on its buys, and its SELL/REDUCE shorts LOST −0.14% a trade, t = −3.3), 12-1 momentum, time-series momentum, low volatility, a 10-month market trend filter, and the NIFTY trend reader that now chooses between buys and puts (selling NIFTY in its downtrends: final year t = 0.21) — all six FAIL. The ranking is built on things that were measured, which is not the same as an edge that was proven. Size accordingly.
